core_obligations: Use the cotangent characterisation of local complete intersections to conclude that NL_{B/A} and NL_{B'/A'} are perfect of tor-amplitude in [-1, 0] (proof lines 22895-22897).

Combine the tensor, pullback-perfect and pullback-tor-amplitude lemmas to show that NL_{B/A} tensor_B B' = NL_{B/A} tensor^L_B B' and that this complex is also perfect of tor-amplitude in [-1, 0] (proof lines 22898-22901).
Choose the distinguished triangle C -> NL_{B/A} tensor_B B' -> NL_{B'/A'} -> C[1] in D(B') (proof lines 22902-22905).
Apply the two-out-of-three and cone-tor-amplitude lemmas to conclude that C is perfect with tor-amplitude in [-1, 1] (proof lines 22906-22908).
Use the base change statement for cotangent complexes to see that C has exactly one nonzero cohomology module, the module of the lemma sitting in degree -1 (proof lines 22908-22910).
Conclude that this module is of finite presentation and flat, hence finite projective (proof lines 22910-22913).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a cocartesian diagram of rings and assumes that A -> B and A' -> B' are local complete intersections in the sense of the section definition; it concludes that the kernel of the comparison map H^{-1}(NL_{B/A} tensor_B B') -> H^{-1}(NL_{B'/A'}) is a finite projective B'-module (source lines 22880-22893). The proof is a structural computation in the derived category. By the cotangent characterisation of local complete intersections, the complexes NL_{B/A} and NL_{B'/A'} are perfect of tor-amplitude in [-1, 0] (proof lines 22895-22897). Combining the tensor, pullback-perfect and pullback-tor-amplitude lemmas, the proof shows that NL_{B/A} tensor_B B' equals the derived tensor product and is also perfect of tor-amplitude in [-1, 0] (proof lines 22898-22901). It then chooses the distinguished triangle C -> NL_{B/A} tensor_B B' -> NL_{B'/A'} -> C[1] in D(B') (proof lines 22902-22905). The substantive step applies the two-out-of-three and cone-tor-amplitude lemmas to conclude that C is perfect with tor-amplitude in [-1, 1] (proof lines 22906-22908), and then uses the base change statement for cotangent complexes to see that C has exactly one nonzero cohomology module, namely the module of the lemma sitting in degree -1 (proof lines 22908-22910). That module is of finite presentation and flat, hence finite projective (proof lines 22910-22913). The non-routine content is the reduction of the statement to a single cohomology module of a perfect complex of known tor-amplitude.
